title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Oil Swell Swamps the Dow
conditions.summary: Stocks fell for a second day as crude jumped about 4% to a six-month high on Middle East tensions. The Dow lost 1.2%, while a chip bounce kept the Nasdaq's loss small.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: The Dow fell 653 points (1.2%) to 52,215, the S&P 500 lost 0.5% to 7,624 and the Nasdaq slipped 0.2% to 25,955.
The Russell 2000 fell 0.3% to 2,776.
Crude oil's jump to a six-month high on Middle East tensions and a tanker strike near Hormuz weighed on stocks.
Chipmakers bounced after Thursday's steep sell-off, but selling spread to staples, industrials and consumer stocks.
Energy led the sectors; consumer staples, industrials and consumer discretionary lagged, and decliners outnumbered advancers.
For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq 0.7%, while the Dow rose 0.4%.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 3.5 basis points to 4.99%, but fell about 11 basis points for the week.
WTI crude rose about 4% to roughly $103 and Brent settled near $116.72; gold fell about 1.2% to near $4,010.
University of Michigan sentiment finished at 48.0, above the 46.3 forecast but near record lows; 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.
October flash PMIs: manufacturing 56.0 beat the 55.5 forecast, services 57.9 was close to the 58.0 forecast.
The Fed meets Oct. 27-28 and is widely expected to hold rates, though futures lean toward a December hike.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: RHI (Robert Half): +13% — beat third-quarter estimates.
CCI (Crown Castle): +12% — reports SpaceX wants to lease about 80,000 U.S. cell sites; SBAC rose nearly 8%.
PANW (Palo Alto Networks): +7% — Evercore ISI survey pointed to stronger security budgets; Cloudflare also gained over 7%.
BE (Bloom Energy): -11% — cash-flow and capex worries despite a beat and raise.
FIX (Comfort Systems USA): -11% — margins below hopes and CFO retirement.
DECK (Deckers): -6% — mixed results, guidance cut and a Piper downgrade.
VZ, T, TMUS (telecoms): lower — worries about SpaceX moving into cell sites.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: American Express beat on profit, missed slightly on revenue and plans about 3,500 job cuts; shares fell about 3%.
Sallie Mae fell about 5% after an unexpected quarterly loss and weak guidance.
RingCentral rose about 7% after beating and raising its full-year outlook.
SLB beat estimates; LKQ fell sharply after withdrawing its full-year guidance.
No major reports after Friday's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: Apple briefly overtook Nvidia as the most valuable U.S. company, both near $5.1 trillion, before Nvidia retook the lead.
Apple launched its foldable iPhone at about $2,000.
SK Hynix shelved a planned U.S. listing for its Solidigm unit, citing market conditions.
Volvo Cars plans to cut 2,500 jobs after a China-driven quarterly operating loss.
Hedge funds had their worst day since the COVID-era rout on Thursday, according to Reuters.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Next session is Monday, Oct. 26: Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 7:30 AM CT and Dallas Fed manufacturing at 9:30 AM CT.
$69 billion 2-year note auction at 12:00 PM CT Monday.
Earnings Monday: Verizon before the open; Cadence Design, Nucor, Celestica and Amkor after the close.
Later in the week: Fed decision Wednesday at 1:00 PM CT, Q3 GDP and PCE inflation Thursday, plus Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Friday, October twenty-third, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking into the water and I'm waxing the board for Monday. Gus the wonder dog spent the afternoon guarding the cooler. Say good evening, Gus! Here's the final set. Choppy water, and a gnarly day for the Dow. The Dow dropped six hundred fifty-three points, or one point two percent, to fifty-two thousand two hundred fifteen. The S and P five hundred slipped one half of one percent to seven thousand six hundred twenty-four. The Nasdaq dipped two tenths of a percent, and the Russell two thousand fell three tenths. Oil was the big swell, jumping about four percent to a six month high on Middle East tensions. Chip stocks bounced after Thursday's wipeout, but staples, industrials and consumer names sank. Energy led, and decliners beat advancers. For the week, the S and P and Nasdaq fell, while the Dow eked out a gain. Wind and weather. The ten year yield rose about three and a half basis points to just under five percent. The dollar firmed, gold slid about one percent, and bitcoin was flat near eighty-one thousand. The VIX rose to about nineteen and a half. Consumer sentiment came in at forty-eight, better than forecast, but near record lows, with inflation expectations rising. The Fed meets next week and is expected to hold rates. Over in the lineup. Robert Half hung ten, up about thirteen percent on a third quarter beat. Gus, that one earned a treat! Here you go, buddy! Crown Castle jumped nearly twelve percent on reports SpaceX wants to lease about eighty thousand cell sites, while the big phone carriers slipped. Palo Alto Networks and Cloudflare gained more than seven percent on an upbeat security survey. On the wipeout side, Bloom Energy and Comfort Systems each fell about eleven percent, and Deckers dropped six percent after a guidance cut. Tide chart. American Express beat on profit but missed slightly on revenue and plans job cuts. The stock fell about three percent. Sallie Mae slid on a surprise loss, while RingCentral rose on a beat and raise. After the bell, a quiet Friday. Beach talk. Apple briefly passed Nvidia as the most valuable U S company, before Nvidia took the Kahuna crown back. Apple also launched a foldable iPhone at about two thousand dollars. And Volvo Cars plans to cut twenty-five hundred jobs. Tomorrow's forecast is really Monday's. The national activity index lands at seven thirty A M Central, and the Dallas Fed survey at nine thirty. Verizon reports before the open, and Cadence Design and Nucor after the close. Then a big week, with the Fed decision Wednesday at one P M Central, plus Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind? Type it in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. That's the last wave of the week. Catch the Dawn Patrol Monday morning. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
